prompt: The audio buyer is checking the cheaper Sonora Pro models. Product names are typed by hand, so the words can appear in any mix of upper and lower case. From the products table, return three columns, in this order: product_id, product_name, unit_cost_eur. Keep only the products whose product_name starts with the text sonora pro (the two words with one space between them), in any letter case, and whose unit_cost_eur is 100 euros or less. Every product has a product_name and a unit_cost_eur. Show unit_cost_eur exactly as stored, without rounding. Return one row per product. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the row filter. Keep a product when its name starts with sonora pro in any letter case and its unit cost is at most 100 euros.
Use the case-blind pattern test on product_name, with a wildcard only where other text may follow. Join it to the cost test with AND, and check whether "or less" keeps 100 itself.
why_this_works: ILIKE ignores letter case, the % after sonora pro allows any model number after it, and <= 100 keeps a product that costs exactly 100 euros.
